Airway: dry cough + breathless + thick/sticky mucus, fever -> bronchial asthma. Rusty/brown phlegm, racing heart, sweats, chills -> pneumonia.

Fever: + stomach pain with diarrhea/constipation -> typhoid; + chills, sweats, muscle aches, itching -> malaria; + headache, pain behind eyes, red spots -> dengue; + fluid-filled itchy bumps -> chicken pox; + sores at nose/mouth oozing yellow crust -> impetigo.

Skin: flaky skin on chest/back leaving marks or stains, hair loss with dandruff, or mood/sexual/cognitive change or tremor -> drug reaction. Altered-color patches with firm nodules -> fungal infection. Silvery scales on knees/elbows, nail dents, joint pain -> psoriasis. Crease rash + slow-healing wounds, thirst, frequent urination -> diabetes.

Yellow skin/eyes + dark urine -> jaundice. Heartburn/sour taste/regurgitation -> gastroesophageal reflux disease. Leg cramps + bulging veins -> varicose veins. Headache + chest pain + dizziness -> hypertension. One-sided headache + light/sound sensitivity -> migraine. Stiff neck/back pain + limb numbness -> cervical spondylosis.

proposals.reason: Probe 3: keeps the parent prompt (best full-validation prompt) and probe 1's label-aware retrieval, only widening the query-neighbor supply from 12 to 20 examples. In coverage layout the 22 label-covering rows are fixed, so this mainly adds query-specific neighbors from the blended ranker; tests whether extra relevant evidence beats extra noise while staying well inside the 12000-char context.

proposals.reason: Probe A: replace the parent's blended lexical ranker with a label-aware ranker. Adds (1) asymmetric document-coverage of the query's rare terms (so a short query cannot be dominated by a verbose partial match, the 0138 failure), (2) per-label signature-cue vectors from train rows with IDF weighting (fever+joint pain should favor dengue over fungal in 0620, 'worse when eating' favors peptic ulcer over GERD in 0214), and (3) label-level smoothed similarity. Everything else, including the prompt, is byte-identical to the incumbent so gains isolate retrieval.

proposals.reason: Probe 4: surgical anti-flooding on the parent's exact ranker and prompt. In coverage layout the one-per-label blocks are fixed by an internal override, so max_per_label=3 only caps the query-neighbor section: at most 3 paraphrases per label (examples=14 leaves room for evidence from more labels). proposals.reason: Retrieval-only probe: identical prompt/config to incumbent, but the ranker now decays a row's score by 0.70^(rank within its label). Failure traces show the trailing neighbor block is monopolized by one wrong label (8 psoriasis rows in 0311, 8 typhoid rows in 0791, mostly fungal rows in 0510), overriding the correct label-coverage row; decay forces the visible neighbor evidence to cover several labels so the query's rare discriminative terms (marks/stains, slow-healing crease wounds, fever+joint pain) decide instead of raw repetition. Label-coverage representatives are unaffected because they are chosen one-per-label.
